name: Question 20
problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14044310/assets/3e065edec23179a946ea28aa6f2b4f9a439ba23c014c38dded0cc7c756867a90.png)

Identify the differential equation that generated the slope field above.
worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14044310/assets/5b92aa0ecaf7dd906a39c44e31a12e725802d9c7c5cdc046351030ae04f6809e.png)

 

Notice the following properties of the given slope field:

- First, the solution curves have vertical asymptotes $x=-1$ and $x=2.$

Of the given equations, the only two that satisfy this condition are

$$
{y}^{′}=\frac{1}{{x}^{2}-x-2}=\frac{1}{(x+1)(x-2)}
$$

 
and

$$
{y}^{′}=\frac{{x}^{2}}{{x}^{2}-x-2}=\frac{{x}^{2}}{(x+1)(x-2)}.
$$

- Second, the slopes of the slope field become horizontal as $x\to \pm \infty .$ 

Of the two remaining options, the only one that gives this behavior is

$$
{y}^{′}=\frac{1}{{x}^{2}-x-2}.
$$

Notice that

$$
{y}^{′}=\frac{1}{{x}^{2}-x-2}\to 0\,\text{as}\,x\to \pm \infty .
$$

Therefore, the slopes of the slope field for the differential equation ${y}^{′}=\frac{1}{{x}^{2}-x-2}$ become horizontal as $x\to \pm \infty .$

On the other hand,

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{{x}^{2}-x-2}=\frac{1}{(1-\frac{1}{x}-\frac{2}{{x}^{2}})}\to 1\,\text{as}\,x\to \pm \infty .
$$

Therefore, the slopes of the slope field for the differential equation ${y}^{′}=\frac{{x}^{2}}{{x}^{2}-x-2}$ do *not* become horizontal as $x\to \pm \infty .$

Question 20
?

Identify the differential equation that generated the slope field above.

a
y′=1x2−x−2
b
y′=1x2−1
c
y′=1x−2
d
y′=x2x2−x−2
e
y′=x2x−2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Notice the following properties of the given slope field:

  • First, the solution curves have vertical asymptotes x=−1 and x=2.

    Of the given equations, the only two that satisfy this condition are y′=1x2−x−2=1(x+1)(x−2) and y′=x2x2−x−2=x2(x+1)(x−2).

  • Second, the slopes of the slope field become horizontal as x→±∞.

    Of the two remaining options, the only one that gives this behavior is y′=1x2−x−2.

    Notice that y′=1x2−x−2→0asx→±∞. Therefore, the slopes of the slope field for the differential equation y′=1x2−x−2 become horizontal as x→±∞.

    On the other hand, x2x2−x−2=1(1−1x−2x2)→1asx→±∞. Therefore, the slopes of the slope field for the differential equation y′=x2x2−x−2 do not become horizontal as x→±∞.
